Small airplane. A place in America’s flying story. ✈️

The Interstate Cadet deserves a little time in the spotlight.

A new October 16 history feature from General Aviation News revisits the two-seat taildragger, developed as the Civilian Pilot Training Program was helping build America’s pool of pilots.

The first production Cadets rolled out in El Segundo, California, in December 1940. More than 300 S-1-A aircraft were delivered into 1942—a reminder that the familiar names weren’t the only companies putting new pilots into the air.

Its story continued with the related L-6 liaison aircraft. The National Museum of the U.S. Air Force preserves an example in Dayton; after military service, surplus L-6s also entered civilian flying.

That’s a general aviation legacy worth remembering: modest airplanes, hands-on flying and a new generation learning what they could do.
